title: Don't buy an EXTENDED WARRANTY: Here's why they suck. | Auto Expert John Cadogan
summary: John Cadogan argues an Australian extended-warranty offer adds little beyond existing consumer-law protection, once its lengthy exclusions are read.

assertions.quote: everything you buy has to be reasonably durable

verdicts.note: True under strong regimes like Australia's Consumer Law; weaker and less consistently enforced in the US, where implied warranties vary by state.
CR notes most products carry an unwritten state-law 'implied warranty of merchantability' requiring them to function as expected and last a reasonable time, independent of any service plan.

assertions.quote: 19 pages of essentially miracle cure for insomnia

verdicts.note: Exclusion lists are commonly extensive, though coverage for named major components still exceeds bare legal guarantees in some jurisdictions.

assertions.quote: if you get the car service somewhere else the contract is void

verdicts.note: A documented contract term in some but not all plans.

assertions.quote: act swiftly this offer expires at the end of June

verdicts.note: Consistent with reported dealership and renewal-letter tactics using artificial deadlines.
